name: T-RAX
summary: A large-effective-area, higher-frequency axion search using a long narrow rectangular waveguide near its cutoff frequency.
detection_principle: A waveguide operates near cutoff, with its narrow cross section controlling the mode and its long area increasing conversion power; a tapered section couples signals to the receiver.

sites.name: Concept proposal; final deployment location undetermined
sites.location: Concept proposal; final deployment location undetermined

status.evidence: 2022 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

collaboration.name: T-RAX Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

results.summary: The paper presents principles, simulations and implementation, without reporting dark-matter results from a completed search.

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.
